title: Do not make Yahweh your enemy

content:
After Israel rejected Yahweh's promise and refused to enter the land of Canaan, God declared the consequences of their unbelief. Although He had forgiven the nation in answer to the prayer of Moses, He would not remove the earthly consequences of their rebellion. Forgiveness did not cancel discipline.

The generation that continually refused to trust Yahweh would not receive the inheritance He had prepared for them. He declared, "Your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness. All who were numbered according to your entire number, from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against Me, shall by no means enter the land" (Numbers 14:29-30).

Notice carefully who came under this judgment. It was directed toward those who had been counted in the military census, every Israelite twenty years old and above who had continually grumbled against God. These were the men who had seen His mighty works with their own eyes, yet again and again refused to believe His Word. But the judgment did not fall upon everyone who came out of Egypt. Joshua and Caleb were specifically spared, because they had trusted Yahweh completely. The tribe of Levi had not been included in the military census, because they were appointed to the service of the Tabernacle rather than to warfare. So many Levites who came out of Egypt were able to enter the land, unless they died for other reasons. Scripture specifically mentions Eleazar serving as High Priest in Canaan, and Ithamar also appears to have survived the wilderness journey. Other Levites entered the land as well, although the Bible does not give us a complete list of their names. Neither did this judgment fall upon those who were under twenty years of age at the time of the census. They had not been counted among the fighting men. A young man who was nineteen years old when Israel stood at Kadesh-barnea would have been nearly sixty years old when the nation finally entered Canaan.

He too had seen the Exodus, crossed the Red Sea, stood at Mount Sinai, eaten the manna, and travelled through the wilderness, yet Yahweh spared him from this particular judgment. And the family of Hobab, the Midianite relative of Moses, also became joined to Israel. His descendants, the Kenites, later settled among the tribe of Judah in Canaan. Although Scripture does not clearly say that Hobab himself entered the land, his family certainly shared in Israel's inheritance.

Yahweh then answered another complaint that the people had spoken in fear. They had said, "Our wives and our little ones will become plunder."

They believed that entering Canaan would lead to the destruction of their children. Yet God replied, "Your little ones, whom you said would become prey, I will bring in, and they shall know the land which you have rejected" (Numbers 14:31). How different Yahweh's thoughts were from the thoughts of the people. The parents imagined that they were protecting their children by refusing to obey. In reality, their unbelief kept them out of the inheritance, while the very children they feared for became the generation that entered the Promised Land. The inheritance they despised became the inheritance their children enjoyed.

God continued, "Your children shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years and shall bear the consequences of your unfaithfulness, until your dead bodies are consumed in the wilderness" (Numbers 14:33). Now here we must be careful. The children were not being punished for their parents' guilt. Scripture consistently teaches that every person answers before Yahweh for his own sin. But children often experience the consequences of the choices their parents make. Because the parents refused to enter Canaan, the children also had to remain in the wilderness for forty years. This shows us an important truth. Sin rarely affects only the one who commits it. A father's rebellion often brings sorrow to his whole family. A mother's unfaithfulness may leave wounds upon her children. The consequences of one generation's choices frequently reach into the next. Yet Yahweh remains perfectly just. He does not condemn innocent children for the guilt of their parents. He simply allows the earthly consequences of sin to continue, while still giving every generation the opportunity to turn to Him.

Then God explained why Israel's wandering would last exactly forty years.
He said, "According to the number of the days in which you spied out the land, forty days, for every day you shall bear your guilt one year, namely forty years" (Numbers 14:34). Forty days of searching the land became forty years of wandering. The punishment perfectly matched the offense. Every day that should have strengthened their faith instead became a year of discipline, because they refused to believe God's promise. And then Yahweh spoke one of the most frightening statements found in the whole wilderness journey.He said, "Then you shall know what it means to have Me against you" (Numbers 14:34). Some translations read, "You shall know My alienation," or, "You shall discover what it is like to have Me for an enemy." These words should make every one of us pause. There is no greater tragedy than to have the living God oppose a person.

Scripture warns us of this solemn truth again and again. The writer to the Hebrews declares, "It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God" (Hebrews 10:31). James teaches, "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble" (James 4:6). And Peter repeats the same words, "God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble" (1 Peter 5:5). When Yahweh fights for His people, no enemy can stand against them. But when Yahweh Himself stands against a person, no human strength can prevail. Israel had once been delivered from Pharaoh because Yahweh fought on their behalf. Now, through their persistent unbelief, they came to know the sorrow of having Yahweh oppose their rebellion. The same God who had been their mighty Defender now stood against them, and there was no power on earth that could change it.

This is a serious warning for every New Creation. We should never live in such a way that Christ becomes opposed to our actions. We make Yahweh our enemy whenever we knowingly resist His will. We make Him our enemy when we continually reject His Word yet still expect His blessing. We make Him our enemy when we harden our hearts against His correction. We make Him our enemy when pride refuses to repent. We make Him our enemy when we persistently choose unbelief over obedience. Yet we must understand that God's opposition is never unfair or unkind. He opposes only what would destroy His people. He resists pride because pride leads to ruin. He disciplines disobedience because He loves His children. He confronts unbelief because unbelief keeps His people from entering the fullness of His promises. His resistance is not the anger of an enemy who wishes us harm. It is the firm hand of a Father who will not allow His child to walk cheerfully toward destruction.

Therefore the New Creation should never presume upon the grace of God while deliberately walking against His revealed will. Instead, we are called to humble ourselves before Him, to receive His correction, and to repent quickly whenever He exposes unbelief in our hearts. And so, at the end of this account, the judgment of Yahweh fell upon the ten spies whose evil report had turned the hearts of the whole nation. Scripture says, "The men whom Moses sent to spy out the land died by a plague before Yahweh" (Numbers 14:36-37). Ten men had spread unbelief, and ten men perished under divine judgment.
Only Joshua and Caleb remained alive. The two who trusted Yahweh lived to receive the inheritance, while the ten who persuaded the people to reject Yahweh never entered it. The contrast could not be clearer. One path was marked by unbelief and ended in death. The other was marked by faith and ended in inheritance.

So the wilderness account leaves every believer with a solemn choice. Will we believe the voice of fear, or will we believe the voice of Yahweh? Will we resist His correction until He must oppose us, or will we humble ourselves beneath His mighty hand? May we never make Yahweh our enemy through pride, unbelief, or persistent rebellion. Instead, let us walk humbly before Him, trusting His promises even when we cannot yet see them fulfilled. For those who walk with Him in faith will discover that the God who disciplines His people is also the God who faithfully brings them into every inheritance He has prepared for them. Israel learned that there is nothing more fearful than to have Yahweh oppose their unbelief. Yet that same God who opposed rebellion faithfully led Joshua, Caleb, and all who trusted Him into the Promised Land. May we walk in humility, faith, and obedience, so that Christ may always be our Advocate and our Shepherd, and never the One who must resist our stubborn hearts.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,
There is no greater tragedy than to have You stand against us, so guard our hearts.

Keep us from resisting Your will, hardening against Your correction, or presuming upon Your grace.

Teach us that Your opposition is never cruelty, but the firm hand of a loving Father.

Help us to humble ourselves quickly beneath Your mighty hand, and to repent without delay.

Let Christ always be our Advocate and Shepherd, and never the One who must resist us.

"Humble yourselves under the mighty power of God, and at the right time he will lift you up in honor." - 1 Peter 5:6

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
